clue.text: A large supermarket stores soft drink

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to store something is to keep it inside, so the supermarket holds the next piece within it

parts.note: the Co-op is a British supermarket chain
p (piano) is the musical marking for playing softly

explanation.surface: A big supermarket keeps a fizzy drink on its shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft drink' reads as one item, but 'soft' belongs to the wordplay and 'drink' alone is the definition. The Co-op is a UK supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcopop is a sweet, fizzy alcoholic beverage sold ready-mixed in bottles.

clue.text: Disengaged attitude in course filling up a year

indicators.note: the course fills the gap between the other letters, so it sits inside them

parts.note: taken as written
a path is a route or course to follow

explanation.surface: Someone describes a slacker's mood while their course occupies a whole year.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is a lack of interest or concern, the outlook of someone who has switched off.

clue.text: In case of collapse, call shrink

indicators.note: the call is placed in the outer letters
a case is the outside shell, so only the first and last letters of the word are kept

parts.note: only its first and last letters, its case, are used
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: Advice that if someone breaks down, you should phone a psychiatrist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrink' looks like slang for a psychiatrist, but here it is a verb meaning to recoil.
explanation.definitionFit: To cringe is to draw back or cower in fear or embarrassment, the same as recoiling.

clue.text: Swans around island with trendy talent for writing

indicators.note: the swans go around the island, enclosing it

parts.note: pens are female swans
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea
hip means fashionable

explanation.surface: Swans circle an island with a fashionable gift for writing.
explanation.walkthrough: A pen is a female swan, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Penmanship is skill in handwriting, a talent for forming letters well.

clue.text: Asked what model did

definitions.meaning: second sense: a model holds a position for an artist or camera

explanation.walkthrough: One word covers both raising a question and sitting still for a portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of a verb meaning both to put forward a question and to hold an attitude for a picture.

clue.text: Peer in entrance to vintner's, one with French cheese

indicators.note: the entrance is the first thing you meet, so take the first letter

parts.note: only its first letter is used
the Roman numeral I
Comté is a hard cheese from the Jura in France

explanation.surface: A nobleman stands at the door of a wine shop holding French cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicomte is a French viscount, a member of the nobility ranking above a baron.

clue.text: Surrogate father perhaps promises to square up

parts.note: a vicar is one example of a priest, who may be called Father
IOUs are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: A stand-in parent pledges to settle the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' is not a parent here but a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicarious means experienced or acting on behalf of another, as a substitute would.

clue.text: Guy making crack

definitions.meaning: first sense: a fellow or man

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a man telling a joke; the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal for a man and also a verb for skin splitting from cold.

clue.text: Source of current trouble, something used by a sailor

parts.note: the mains supply provides electric current
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A sailor's equipment blamed for an electrical fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' tempts toward water and tides, but here it is electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainsail is the principal sail of a vessel, which a sailor rigs and trims.

clue.text: Anteater, say, in gallery at the back of garden

indicators.note: the gallery comes after the garden, placed behind it

parts.note: the Garden of Eden
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: An anteater is spotted in an art gallery behind the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentates are an old order of toothless mammals, of which the anteater is an example.

clue.text: Like a Scot, or possibly Japanese

parts.note: as means in the manner of
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person is Scottish or Japanese.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese person is one example of someone from the continent of Asia.

clue.text: Thus spies possibly skinny party grandee?

parts.note: so means in this way
the CIA is the American intelligence agency
lite, as on a low-fat product, is one sense of skinny, as in a skinny latte

explanation.surface: Wondering if thin spies make for a senior party figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party grandee' suggests a political heavyweight; here the party is a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A socialite is a prominent figure in fashionable society, a big name at gatherings.

clue.text: Bereft of assistance, drunk as well as sober

parts.note: high means intoxicated
and joins two things
dry means abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: A paradox: someone being both drunk and sober at once, and left helpless.
explanation.definitionFit: Left high and dry means stranded without help, like a boat beached by the tide.

clue.text: Utterance seeking attention in extremely pretentious way

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: only its first and last letters are used
St is short for Street

explanation.surface: Someone tries to catch another's eye in a showy manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Psst is the whispered sound used to draw someone's notice discreetly.

clue.text: List and track staff in community organisation

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties
Ry is short for railway
a club is a heavy stick

explanation.surface: Listing workers and monitoring employees in a local body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' suggests employees; here it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotary Club is a branch of an international service association of business people.

clue.text: One getting free case loaded with game meat

indicators.note: loaded means drunk, so the letters of the case reel into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder
polo is a game played on horseback
the meat of an argument is its gist

explanation.surface: Someone receives a crate stuffed with venison or pheasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded with' reads as packed full, but 'loaded' is an anagram signal and 'game meat' splits into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapologist is a performer like Houdini who frees himself from chains and boxes.

clue.text: Attending entertaining party, people feeling embarrassed

definitions.note: a noun phrase here: the feeling of being embarrassed

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them inside, so the other letters go within

parts.note: at means present at, as at a concert
a bash is a party
men, people in general

explanation.surface: Guests at a party feel awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Abashment is the state of shame or discomfiture, a sense of being embarrassed.

clue.text: Fresh mint chopped around sweet course, ultimately

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the dessert
chopped herbs are cut up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder
pud is short for pudding, a dessert

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take the last letter

parts.note: only its last letter is used

explanation.surface: A recipe step: chopped mint scattered over a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet course' looks like one phrase for dessert, but 'sweet' alone gives the pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh in the sense of cheeky or forward, just as an impudent person is.

clue.text: Media hasn't succeeded with old forecast

indicators.note: lacking the next piece, so it is removed

parts.note: the press is the news media
aged means old

explanation.surface: The newspapers missed a long-ago prediction.
explanation.definitionFit: Presaged means foretold or foreshadowed, a verb in the past tense matching forecast.

clue.text: Alarming changes ready to overwhelm a nervous MP here?

indicators.note: changes means the letters are altered into another order

parts.note: anagram fodder

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so the ready word surrounds the single letter

parts.note: set means ready, as in ready, steady, go
taken as written

explanation.surface: Worrying swings are poised to swamp an anxious politician.
explanation.walkthrough: A marginal seat is a UK constituency won by a narrow majority, where the sitting MP has most to fear.
explanation.definitionFit: A marginal seat is one with a slim majority, where an MP might well feel insecure.

clue.text: African from really African country

parts.note: so means very, as in so tired
Mali is a landlocked West African nation

explanation.surface: A person from a very African nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Somali is a native of Somalia in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Bit of song? Song's intro, obviously

indicators.note: the intro of a song is its opening, so take the first letter

parts.note: only its first letter is used
natch is slang for naturally, of course

explanation.surface: A snippet of a tune: the opening, naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: A snatch of song is a brief fragment of it, a short excerpt heard in passing.

clue.text: Queen covered by country stars

indicators.note: the monarch sits under cover of the country, inside it

parts.note: the USA
R for Regina

explanation.surface: A monarch is protected by a nation's celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursa Major and Ursa Minor are constellations, groups of stars named after bears.

clue.text: A number of sailors have to accept time in slum

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the time goes inside the combined words

parts.note: a shanty is a song, a number, sung by sailors
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Some sailors must put up with a spell in a run-down district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is a song, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A shanty town is a settlement of makeshift shacks, a poor and squalid neighbourhood.

clue.text: Refusal and agreement? Flipping curious!

parts.note: no is a refusal

indicators.note: to flip something turns it over, so the agreement is read backwards

parts.note: yes signals agreement

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry about someone saying no and yes, wanting to know too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British oath, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosey means prying or inquisitive, too interested in others' business.

clue.text: Drive from centre of Thurso, say, northwards

indicators.note: the centre is the middle, so take the middle letters

parts.note: a town on the north coast of Scotland; only its middle letters are used

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: e.g., for example

explanation.surface: A motorist heads north out of the middle of a Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive as a noun means a strong impulse or motivation, the same as an urge.

clue.text: Cooked greens, in the main, rolled around in relish

indicators.note: the sea goes around the cooked letters
rolled means one letter rolls from the front to the back

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open sea

indicators.note: cooking alters the greens, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A recipe: greens cooked mostly then rolled, served in a condiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relish' looks like a sauce, but here it means keen enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: Relish as a noun is zest or keen enjoyment, the same as eagerness.

clue.text: Did a spring clean naked? Choose to conceal nothing

indicators.note: stripped of its outer layer, so the first and last letters are lost

parts.note: only its inner letters are used

indicators.note: hiding the zero makes it vanish from the word

parts.note: to opt is to choose

explanation.surface: A spring clean done without clothes, choosing to keep nothing hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring clean' reads as a household chore, but 'Did a spring' is the definition and 'clean' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapt is the past tense of leap, meaning jumped or sprang into the air.

clue.text: Most ordered tea, we hear, that is taken around one

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that sounds like the letter needed

parts.note: sounds like the letter T

indicators.note: the Latin phrase is put around the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: id est is Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.
the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone asks for tea, and it is brought round to one person.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidiest is the superlative of tidy, meaning neatest or most orderly.

clue.text: Uncouth child withdrawing before blunder

indicators.note: the first part comes ahead of the second
withdrawing means pulling back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a boy is a child
bish is British slang for a mistake

explanation.surface: A rude kid retreats ahead of making a gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: A yob is a British word for a lout; bish is dated British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Yobbish means loutish or boorish, behaving like a hooligan.
